newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool seen continuing downward trend.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool seen continuing downward trend.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue their downward trend this week, pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly wool report.

Sales this week are in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with 108,000 bales on offer. The eastern market indicator last week closed down 18 cents at 589 cents a kg clean. The western market indicator closed at 531 cents a kg, down 11 cents.

"The short term outlook indicates a gradual continuation of this downward trend with a very supply driven environment, restrained only by grower resistance to lower prices," the Wesfarmers Dalgety report said.
"For the next few weeks rostered quantities remain large, swamping the limited demand and, coupled with this, buyers are now limiting activity in anticipated of a cheaper market."

Wesfarmers said the market for stylish, fine wool was not expected to follow this easing trend because they were in limited supply owing to a general broadening of the clip (by 0.5 micron) with the better seasonal conditions.
